newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end weaker but outperform dlr bloc.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end weaker but outperform dlr bloc.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.70 PCT (PREV 7.75) US 5-YR 6.39 (PREV 6.27)
* NZ bonds end weaker but outperform dollar bloc
* Money market softer as TWI slips from highs
* Market bullish heading into CPI, downside potential seen
New Zealand bonds finished slightly weaker on Monday but managed to outperform a U.S. Treasury market hit by surprisingly strong December job growth.
"The market again was better bid than what one would have thought given the sell-off in U.S. Treasuries after non-farm payrolls figures," one bond dealer said.
"From here I think we tend to be stuck within a range following the U.S. but outperforming the U.S. each time it either sells off or likewise turns around and becomes a little bit bid."

The dealer said there had been very little price action in the trader market after the open, and all was quiet on the institutional front as well. Bonds closed four to five points weaker across the curve.

In the money market, 90-day bank bills ended five basis points weaker at 7.53 percent after selling off to 7.57 percent as the currency's Trade-Weighted Index fell. The TWI closed around 67.90 from its 68.19 open.
Sentiment was fairly strong going into key inflation data due on Friday. One bill dealer said that with the TWI around 68, the 90-days could settle quite happily around 7.35 percent.
If the TWI averaged 68.20 percent over the quarter, then according to Reserve Bank forecasts the 90-days could be around 7.19 percent, the dealer said.
"So at 7.55-7.56 percent which it got up to this morning it's still obviously fairly attractive...Basically the market should be fairly comfortable with the bills."
The dealer said any hawkish comment from the Reserve Bank about falling interest rates would send the already firm currency through the ceiling.
